payload.title: Average Wedding Photographer Cost and What Packages Include
payload.excerpt: What shapes a wedding photographer's quote, what a package should spell out in writing, the extras that sit outside it, questions to settle for a wedding abroad, and your consumer and copyright position in Australia before you sign.
key_takeaways: Coverage, team, travel, albums and image rights shape a photographer's quote far more than any national average, so ask every photographer to quote against the same written brief.
Compare quotes line by line on what is written down: hours, people, deliverables, delivery timing, licence and extras.
In Australia, a couple who commissions and pays for wedding photos owns the copyright by default under section 35(5) of the Copyright Act 1968, but the agreement can exclude or modify that rule.
Under the consumer guarantees, a photographer must use an acceptable level of care and skill, and those basic rights can't be taken away by anything the business says or does.

faq.q: Why don't you give an average cost for a wedding photographer?
faq.a: Because a national average blends very different weddings, and a figure built from other people's days can't tell you what yours will cost. Send several photographers the same written brief, then use the comparison steps above to read their quotes side by side.

faq.q: How much should I pay for a photographer?
faq.a: We don't suggest a figure, because the right spend depends on the hours, people and products your day needs. Decide which moments matter, what coverage and team that takes and what you want to hold at the end, then compare quotes that match on those points.

faq.q: What do wedding photographer packages include?
faq.a: A clear package states coverage hours, the photographers involved, any pre-wedding session, the online gallery, the expected number of edited images, delivery dates, album and print specifications, usage and copyright, and a backup plan. Anything not written down should be treated as not included.

faq.q: Who owns the copyright in our wedding photos?
faq.a: As at November 2026, under [section 35(5)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ca1968133/s35.html) of the Copyright Act 1968, a person who pays for a photograph taken for a private or domestic purpose owns the copyright, and section 35(7) names a wedding party as a private or domestic purpose. The agreement can exclude or modify that rule, so read the usage and copyright clause before you sign.

faq.q: How far ahead should we book a wedding photographer?
faq.a: As soon as your date and venue are confirmed, because a photographer can only be in one place on any given day. For a wedding abroad, allow time to settle travel and accommodation in the contract too.
